title: Spacetime Dynamics of Altermagnetic Magnons
authors: Ali Emami Kopaei, Karthik Subramaniam Eswaran, Krzysztof Wohlfeld
abstract: Distinguishing altermagnetism from conventional ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism typically relies on momentum-space probes. Here, we show that the real-space spreading of a localized spin excitation provides a distinctive dynamical fingerprint of altermagnetic order. Using linear spin-wave theory on a two-dimensional checkerboard lattice with nearest-neighbor and next-nearest-neighbor couplings J_1 and J_2, we demonstrate that finite J_2 produces direction-dependent magnon group velocities and splits the two magnon branches. The resulting propagation remains closer to that of an antiferromagnet than a ferromagnet, retaining an approximately circular outer wavefront, while the direction-dependent magnon velocities produce a pronounced cross-like spatial structure inside this front. We further show that changing the sign of J_2 to enter the unfrustrated regime (J_2<0) increases the characteristic propagation velocities and interchanges the diagonal directions of enhanced propagation, corresponding to a pi/2 rotation of the anisotropic spatial pattern. These results establish spacetime dynamics as a complementary probe of altermagnetic magnons, providing a route to identifying unconventional magnetic order through real-space propagation patterns in solid-state and synthetic quantum systems.
summary: This theoretical work establishes that the real-space propagation pattern of a localized spin excitation serves as a unique fingerprint for altermagnetic order. By analyzing the time evolution of magnons on a 2D lattice, the authors show that the resulting spatial structure—a cross-like pattern—is distinct from both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic counterparts. This provides a powerful, complementary method for identifying unconventional magnetic states in quantum materials.
main_problem: To find a distinctive dynamical fingerprint of altermagnetic order, moving beyond conventional momentum-space probes.
main_result: The real-space spreading of a localized spin excitation reveals a cross-like structure inside the wavefront, distinguishing altermagnetism from ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism.
method: Linear spin-wave theory is applied to calculate the time evolution of a localized spin excitation, tracking its real-space probability density.
model_or_system: The study uses a Heisenberg model on a 2D checkerboard lattice with nearest-neighbor ($J_1$) and next-nearest-neighbor ($J_2$) couplings, modeling altermagnetic magnets.
key_observables: Real-space density profile $ho(r, t)$ of the spin excitation, magnon group velocities $v_{\sigma}(k)$, and the resulting spatial pattern.
important_parameters: The ratio $J_2/J_1$, and the sign of $J_2$ (frustrated vs. unfrustrated regimes).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on linear spin-wave theory, which approximates the Hamiltonian up to quadratic order in bosonic operators.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate magnon dispersion splitting due to $J_2$, and density profiles showing the characteristic cross-like structure in the altermagnetic regime, compared to square (FM) or circular (AFM) fronts.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the Hamiltonian and using spin-wave theory to find magnon dispersion. It then calculates the time evolution of a localized excitation, comparing the resulting real-space density patterns across FM, AFM, and altermagnetic regimes, concluding with the physical interpretation of the results.
why_interesting: The focus on real-space, time-domain dynamics (wave packet spreading) provides a novel diagnostic tool for characterizing magnetic order, which is highly relevant for understanding complex many-body ground states in correlated materials.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. (a) Schematic representation of the Heisenberg model on a 2D checkerboard lattice featuring collinear Ne´el order. The A and B sublattices are connected by a compos- ite symmetry operation consisting of a mirror reflection and a spin inversion. (b) Magnon dispersion relations ωk for the next-nearest-neighbor Heisenberg exchange J2 = 0.2 (with the nearest neighbor exchange J1 = 1). The introduction of next-nearest-neighbor coupling J2 unequivocally lifts the band degeneracy across the Brillouin zone, except along the high-symmetry nodal axes (kx = 0, ky = 0) where the degen- eracy is protected by the lattice symmetry.

FIG. 3. Magnitude of the magnon group velocity, |vσ(k)|, across the Brillouin zone. (a) In the antiferromagnetic limit, J2 = 0, the largest group velocities are distributed nearly isotropically around the Γ point. (b) For finite J2 > 0, this distribution becomes direction dependent, with the largest ve- locities concentrated along selected diagonal directions. This deformation of the group-velocity distribution reflects the di- rection dependence of the altermagnetic magnon dispersion discussed in the main text. The parameters are (a) θ = 0 (J1 = 1, J2 = 0) and (b) θ = 0.3 (J1 ≃0.95, J2 ≃0.29), with σ = −1.

FIG. 2. Comparison of the real-space spreading of a single-site spin-flip excitation in the absence of next-nearest- neighbor interactions (J2 = 0). (a) In the ferromagnetic case (J1 < 0), the largest group velocities occur at finite momenta, making the propagation sensitive to short-wavelength, lattice- scale physics and producing the characteristic square-shaped density profile. (b) In the antiferromagnetic case (J1 > 0), the largest group velocities occur in the long-wavelength regime, where the linear magnon dispersion is approximately rotation- ally symmetric. The resulting wavefront is therefore nearly circular and much less sensitive to the underlying square- lattice structure.

FIG. 4. Time-resolved spatial density profiles following a single-site spin flip in the representative altermagnetic regime, θ = 0.3 (J1 ≃0.95, J2 ≃0.29), at t = 2.0, 11.5, 22.0, and 42.0. The outer propagation front remains approximately circular, reflecting the dominant antiferromagnetic-like propagation, while the direction-dependent base dispersion and the altermagnetic branch splitting produce a cross-like structure inside the wave packet. Panels (a) and (b) show the σ = +1 and σ = −1 magnon branches, respectively. The lattice size is N = 200.

FIG. 5. Time-resolved spatial density profiles following a single-site spin flip in the unfrustrated altermagnetic regime, θ = −0.4 (J1 ≃0.92, J2 ≃−0.38), at t = 2.0, 11.5, 22.0, and 42.0. Compared with the frustrated regime shown in Fig. 4, the wave packet spreads considerably farther and its anisotropic spatial pattern is rotated by π/2. These changes reflect the larger characteristic magnon group velocities for J2 < 0 and the reversal of the branch-dependent altermagnetic contribution discussed in the main text. Panels (a) and (b) show the σ = +1 and σ = −1 magnon branches, respectively. The lattice size is N = 200.
